_about: Raw MCP stdio exchange between week9/agent.py's client and the claims-system server, captured by week9/capture_wire.py (verbatim lines in evidence/wire_raw.jsonl). 'raw' is the exact line on the wire; 'parsed' is the same line decoded for reading; 'annotations' explains every top-level field by hand.
transport: stdio: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on the server's stdin/stdout; the server's stderr is a separate log channel (week9/logs/claims_system.stderr.log), never part of the protocol.
model_call_location: The model is called only in the host (week9/agent.py, _groq_call -> Groq HTTPS), BEFORE step 6 to choose the tool and AFTER step 7 to read the result; nowhere on this wire and never inside either MCP server.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag; MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0, so every message carries exactly "2.0".
annotations.id: Request id 1, chosen by the client. The server must echo it so the reply can be matched; its presence makes this a request that needs an answer.
annotations.method: "initialize" must be the first message on a new connection: version and capability negotiation before anything else.
annotations.params: protocolVersion = the MCP spec revision the client speaks (2025-06-18); capabilities = what the CLIENT offers the server (empty: no sampling, roots or elicitation, so the server cannot ask our host to run a model); clientInfo = name/version of the host for the server's logs.

annotations.id: Echoes 1, so this is the answer to the initialize request.
annotations.result: protocolVersion = the version the server agreed to (same as asked, so the session proceeds); capabilities = what the SERVER offers: only tools (listChanged:false = the tool list will not change mid-session; no resources, no prompts); serverInfo = claims-system 0.4.2, the third-party build we are trusting.

annotations.method: "notifications/initialized": the client confirms the handshake is complete and normal operation may begin. No id, so it is a notification and gets no reply.
"tools/list": discovery. The host asks what the server can do instead of hard-coding it. No params, so this is the first page (no cursor).

tools.name: get_claim_status
tools.description: Get the current status of one insurance claim by claim number: status (pending, under_review, escalated, approved, partial_settlement, denied), claimant, policy number, declared damage type, declared amount, policy excess, submitted date, last update and assigned adjuster. Claim numbers look like CLM-YYYY-nnnnn. Does not return adjuster notes.

tools.name: get_adjuster_note_history
tools.description: Get the full adjuster note history for one claim, oldest first. Each entry has date, stage (pending, reviewed, escalated, denied), adjuster and the note text. Later stages supersede earlier ones: an 'escalated' note confirms or overturns a provisional 'reviewed' finding. Claim numbers look like CLM-YYYY-nnnnn.

annotations.result: tools = 2 tool definitions (get_claim_status, get_adjuster_note_history), each with name, description (the text the MODEL reads to decide when to call it) and inputSchema (JSON Schema for the arguments; claim_number pattern ^CLM-\d{4}-\d{5}$). No nextCursor, so this is the complete list. The host turns these into model tool schemas named claims_system__<tool>.

annotations.method: "tools/call": execute one tool. In the agent this is sent only after the model asked for it; the host routes it here.
annotations.params: name = the server-local tool name (get_claim_status, without the claims_system__ prefix the model saw); arguments = the arguments object, validated by the server (claim_number CLM-2024-88102).

annotations.result: content = list of content blocks; here one text block holding the claim status as JSON (status escalated, claimant, amounts, adjuster). isError:false = the tool ran successfully. A failed lookup comes back here too, as isError:true with a readable message, not as a JSON-RPC error, so the model can see it and recover.
